title: 416550 - Postdoctoral Appointee - CSE - Heavy Element Chemistry and Separation Science Group

cond_0001.intro: The Heavy Element Chemistry and Separation Science group in the Chemical Sciences & Engineering Division at [Company name masked] has an opening for a Postdoctoral Appointee to conduct fundamental research centered on liquid surfaces/interfaces. As part of an ongoing program in chemical separations the position integrates advanced techniques in surface science with inorganic, analytical, and physical chemistries. The successful candidate will contribute to a vibrant multidisciplinary team addressing questions important to the nation's energy management. The position includes the freedom to participate in all aspects of project development, data acquisition, and interpretation. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to report original results at scientific conferences and in peer-reviewed literature.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Degree with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent
Considerable knowledge of data analysis methods
Considerable skill in both written and oral communication, and the ability to work interactively and productively in a multidisciplinary environment
Preferred Requirements
Experience with surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques, including second-harmonic generation (SHG), sum-frequency generation (SFG), and phase sensitive SFG
Practical expertise in surface-sensitive measurements, including tensiometry of liquid-vapor interfaces and Langmuir trough techniques, as well as experience with surface functionalization and self-assembled monolayer preparation
Some knowledge of high-resolution synchrotron-based X-ray scattering and spectroscopy techniques (such as X-ray reflectivity and X-ray absorption spectroscopy)
Some knowledge of analytical chemistry, chemical separations, or interfacial processes

As part of an ongoing program in chemical separations the position integrates advanced techniques in surface science with inorganic, analytical, and physical chemistries. The successful candidate will contribute to a vibrant multidisciplinary team addressing questions important to the nation's energy management. The position includes the freedom to participate in all aspects of project development, data acquisition, and interpretation. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to report original results at scientific conferences and in peer-reviewed literature.
cond_0102.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree in chemistry or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, with around 0 to 3 years of experience
Ideally, we are seeking a chemist with some experience with surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques, including second-harmonic generation (SHG), sum-frequency generation (SFG), and phase sensitive SFG; candidates still building familiarity in these areas are welcome to apply
A working knowledge of data analysis methods is expected
Experience with surface-sensitive measurements, including tensiometry of liquid-vapor interfaces and Langmuir trough techniques would be an asset, as would exposure to surface functionalization and self-assembled monolayer preparation
Some background in high-resolution synchrotron-based X-ray scattering and spectroscopy techniques (such as X-ray reflectivity and X-ray absorption spectroscopy) may be viewed as a plus
Some background in analytical chemistry, chemical separations or interfacial processes would provide a strong advantage
Ability to communicate effectively in both written and oral forms is considered a strength, as is a willingness to work interactively and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment

Ph.D. In chemistry or a related field with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent

The successful candidate will contribute to a vibrant multidisciplinary team addressing questions important to the nation's energy management. The position includes the freedom to participate in all aspects of project development, data acquisition, and interpretation. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to report original results at scientific conferences and in peer-reviewed literature. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of surface science and interfacial chemistry.
cond_0346.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Degree with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent
Considerable knowledge of data analysis methods
Considerable skill in both written and oral communication, and the desire to work interactively and productively in a multidisciplinary environment
Preferred Requirements
Experience with surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques, including second-harmonic generation (SHG), sum-frequency generation (SFG), and phase sensitive SFG
Practical expertise in surface-sensitive measurements, including tensiometry of liquid-vapor interfaces and Langmuir trough techniques, as well as experience with surface functionalization and self-assembled monolayer preparation
Some knowledge of high-resolution synchrotron-based X-ray scattering and spectroscopy techniques (such as X-ray reflectivity and X-ray absorption spectroscopy)
Some knowledge of analytical chemistry, chemical separations, or interfacial processes

The successful candidate will contribute to a vibrant multidisciplinary team addressing questions important to the nation's energy management. The position includes the freedom to participate in all aspects of project development, data acquisition, and interpretation. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to report original results at scientific conferences and in peer-reviewed literature.
cond_0362.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Degree in chemistry or a closely related field required; 0 to 3 years of demonstrated expertise beyond doctoral training
Deep knowledge of data analysis methods applicable to surface science and spectroscopic data
Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with a proven ability to work interactively and productively in a multidisciplinary environment
Preferred Requirements
Strong command of surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques, including second-harmonic generation (SHG), sum-frequency generation (SFG), and phase-sensitive SFG
Substantial practical expertise in surface-sensitive measurements, including tensiometry of liquid-vapor interfaces and Langmuir trough techniques, as well as surface functionalization and self-assembled monolayer preparation
Solid understanding of high-resolution synchrotron-based X-ray scattering and spectroscopy techniques, such as X-ray reflectivity and X-ray absorption spectroscopy
Advanced knowledge of analytical chemistry, chemical separations, or interfacial processes

You will be an active part of a multidisciplinary team addressing questions important to the nation's energy management, regularly contributing to all aspects of project development, data acquisition, and interpretation. You will also have the opportunity to present original results at scientific conferences and in peer-reviewed literature.
cond_0501.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree level with 0 to 3 years of experience or equivalent
Ideally, we are seeking a chemist with experience with surface-sensitive spectroscopic techniques, including second-harmonic generation (SHG), sum-frequency generation (SFG), and phase sensitive SFG
Considerable knowledge of data analyses methods is expected
Practical expertise in surface-sensitive measurements, including tensiometry of liquid-vapor interfaces and Langmuir trough techniques would be an asset, as would experience with surface functionalization and self-assembled monolayer preparation
Some knowledge of high-resolution synchrotron-based X-ray scattering and spectroscopy techniques (such as X-ray reflectivity and X-ray absorption spectroscopy) may be viewed as a plus
Some knowledge of analytical chemistry, chemical separations or interfacial processes would provide a strong advantage
Considerable skill in both written and oral communication is considered a strength, as is the ability to work interactively and productively with others in a multidisciplinary environment
